title: Reliability Transit Sprint Manifest: cross-functional handoff and SLO runway
body:
Purpose and constraints:
This manifest documents a 6-week cross-functional reliability sprint (the 'Transit Sprint') whose primary objective is to move SLOs for model-serving features from proposal into operational ownership. Transit means transition: we intentionally design activities so that product feature teams, serving-runtime, platform-engineering, and SREs share clear handoff gates, telemetry contracts, and mitigation runbooks.

Scope and success criteria:
- Scope: three pilot services (chat-api, batch-embeddings, and streaming-inference) and their end-to-end SLOs (availability, P99 latency, and inference-error-rate).
- Success: each service has an agreed SLO definition, alerting thresholds wired into the observability pipeline, a documented mitigation playbook, and a staffed oncall rotation for the first 90 days after handoff.
- Acceptance checks: SLO definitions committed in Confluence, synthetic tests running for 7 consecutive days with no signal gaps, and a canary rollout plan approved by product owners.

Sprint structure (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (Prep): instrumentation gap analysis, stakeholder alignment, baseline telemetry capture (sample window 7 days). Owners: platform-engineering + product-hosted-api.
- Week 1–2 (Design and Contracts): finalize SLO formulas, define error budget policies, map dimensionality (region, model-size, route), draft observability events and tracing tags. Owners: product + serving-runtime + obs.
- Week 3 (Implementation): wire metrics to the vendor/stack (Prometheus exporters, tracing spans), add synthetic canaries, and set alert rules in the alerting stack. Owners: platform-engineering + observability.
- Week 4 (Exercise & Playbook): run tabletop for incidents, validate playbooks, refine escalation matrix and runbook steps. Owners: SRE + platform-engineering.
- Week 5 (Handoff & Canary): run a controlled traffic canary with rollback triggers, finalize oncall handoffs and knowledge transfer sessions. Owners: service feature teams + SRE.
- Week 6 (Stabilize & Retro): monitor error budget burn, finalize post-handoff monitoring checklist, retro and next-steps. Owners: all stakeholders.

Milestones and deliverables (mapped to weeks):
- M0 (end of Week 0): Instrumentation gap doc + baseline metrics snapshot.
- M1 (end of Week 2): SLO spec for each pilot (yaml/Confluence link) and alert policy draft.
- M2 (end of Week 3): Observable pipeline wired; synthetic checks producing green signals.
- M3 (end of Week 5): Canary completed, runbooks & oncall roster published.
- M4 (end of Week 6): Final sign-off and transfer ticket to operational cadence.

RACI at a glance:
- Responsible: platform-engineering (instrumentation, alerting), serving-runtime (compatibility & perf data), observability (dashboards, synthetic checks).
- Accountable: SRE manager for overall acceptance; product manager for SLO targets.
- Consulted: solutions-eng (customer-facing SLA implications), legal/compliance (if customer contractual SLOs affected).
- Informed: GTM/customer-success for external comms readiness.

Telemetry & observability contract (short form):
Each service owner must expose the following metrics with stable labels:
- request_total{route,region,model_variant} (counter)
- request_latency_ms{quantile,route,region} (histogram)
- inference_errors_total{type,route,region} (counter)
Tracing must include root span annotation 'model.variant' and 'request.origin'. Synthetic canary: a single-step inference check every 1m per region.

Runbooks (examples):
- P99 latency spike: immediate mitigation = route replacement to smaller model_variant; if no improvement in 5 min, throttle burst traffic to 50% and open incident bridge.
- Availability degradation: check serving pool health, rotate nodes using rollout script, failover to fallback region.
Each runbook must list pre-approved rollback commands and 2-minute triage checklist.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Missing labels or inconsistent metric cardinality. Mitigation: strict schema linter and a pre-merge CI check. Owner: platform-eng.
- Risk: Canary traffic causes customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: traffic caps, feature-flagged rollouts, immediate rollback triggers. Owner: product + SRE.
- Risk: Error-budget policy too aggressive causing alert fatigue. Mitigation: calibration trial in Week 2, synthetic burn tests. Owner: SRE.

Communication plan and rituals:
- Daily 15-min standup for the sprint team (M-F) during Weeks 1–5.
- Weekly cross-functional sync with PM, SRE lead, platform-eng, and serving-runtime lead.
- Decision log maintained in Confluence; all gating decisions require at least two approvers (SRE manager + PM).
- Slack channel: #transit-sprint-rel (updates, blockers, incident pings).

Handoff checklist (must be complete for signoff):
1) SLO spec checked into Confluence and referenced in service repo.
2) Alerts are firing into the ops channel and pagers tested.
3) Synthetic checks cover all targeted regions and models.
4) Runbooks published and validated in a live tabletop.
5) Oncall shifts and rotation documented in schedule.
6) Post-handoff 90-day monitoring plan created (signal cadence & owners).

Measurement and short-term KPIs:
- Time to detect (MTTD) for injected faults during tabletop ≤ 3 minutes.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for simulated latency spikes ≤ 12 minutes.
- False positive alert rate < 15% during the stabilization week.
- SLO definition approval from product & SRE by end of Week 2 (binary pass/fail).

Budget and staffing assumptions:
- Dedicated 0.5 FTE platform-eng lead, 0.5 FTE observability engineer, 1.0 FTE SRE coverage (for runbook design & tabletop). Product: 0.2 PM support. Additional SOL budget for canary-related burst capacity estimated at $4k for cloud GPUs across test windows.

Open questions and decisions needed now:
- Should the streaming-inference SLO include per-token latency or end-to-end response time? (Decision owner: product + serving-runtime)
- Exact cardinality limits for model_variant labels (target max 30 variants per route).
- Canary traffic percentage thresholds for each service (recommended: start at 1% then 10%).

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Platform-eng: run metric-schema linter against pilot repos (owner: Evan Chen).
- Observability: deploy synthetic canary scaffold to test cluster (owner: Priya Desai).
- SRE: draft incident playbook templates for P99/availability cases (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- PM: schedule two 30-minute alignment sessions with feature leads and legal (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Notes to reviewers:
- This document is intentionally prescriptive around gates to avoid ambiguous "handovers". Expect iterative updates; please add comments inline in Confluence (linked_artifacts). If you disagree with any mitigation or owner, flag it and propose an alternate owner.

Appendix: quick checklist for the first tabletop exercise
- Confirm synthetic canary is green for 48 hours.
- Inject latency into a replica pool and record MTTD/MTTM.
- Execute latency mitigation (model_variant swap) and measure rollback fidelity.
- Validate alert routing to the oncall channel and confirm paging behavior.

Document history:
- 2026-01-15: initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-01-22: added telemetry contract and risk register (collaborators updated).
- 2026-02-02: refined staffing assumptions and canary steps after platform-eng review.
